# Biocon Limited

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-30 · status **partial** · Primary source biocon.com (annual reports, CSR annexures, BRSR, CSR policy, Foundation site) and LinkedIn/Facebook were all HELD by robots.txt/registry rules; usable public figures were limited to one India CSR news summary of the FY2023-24 annexure plus two feature articles on Biocon Foundation's programmes. Search budget spent before FY2022-23 and FY2024-25 statutory figures could be located from a readable source.

Biocon Limited (CIN L24234KA1978PLC003417, BSE 532523/NSE BIOCON) is a Section 135-bound CSR funder; its CSR is implemented principally through Biocon Foundation (est. 2004, Managing Trustee Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw), a distinct entity recorded here with parent_name Biocon Limited. Only one readable source (India CSR) gave a statutory-style figure: combined Biocon Group (Biocon Limited + Biocon Biologics + Syngene) FY2023-24 CSR spend of Rs. 31.54 crore, of which Biocon Limited's own share was Rs. 5.09 crore across healthcare, education, rural development/women empowerment and environment, reaching 3.75 lakh beneficiaries group-wide. Feature articles describe Biocon Foundation programmes (eLAJ Smart Clinics, Arogya Raksha Yojana, oral cancer mHealth screening, Biocon Nagar housing, Hebbagodi/Yarandahalli lake rejuvenation, Hebbagodi Metro funding, Biocon Academy) concentrated in Karnataka, with cumulative reach of 2.8 million lives since 2004. No FY2022-23 or FY2024-25 statutory annexure figures (prescribed CSR, average net profit, unspent, impact assessment), no Foundation-specific identifiers, no named third-party implementing NGOs, no published CSR mailbox and no confirmed open RFP were reachable within budget — all sit behind HELD biocon.com/LinkedIn/Facebook pages or a 403 (fundsforngos.org).

Website: https://www.biocon.com

## What it set out to find

- identity and identifiers (CIN/PAN/CSR-1) for Biocon Limited and Biocon Foundation, and their parent/foundation relationship
- funder_csr_years for FY2024-25, FY2023-24, FY2022-23 (obligation, prescribed/spent CSR, unspent, impact assessment)
- funder_csr_spend by sector/state/district/implementing agency
- footprints (districts/states where money actually went)
- named partners/implementing agencies by year
- programs run by Biocon/Biocon Foundation
- metrics/beneficiaries/outcomes
- published CSR contact mailbox
- documents (CSR annexure, annual report, BRSR, foundation site)
- open RFPs / partner-with-us calls

## Programmes

- **Arogya Raksha Yojana (ARY) · programme · under Biocon Foundation**
  > The Arogya Raksha Yojana (ARY): A pioneering microinsurance program offering affordable healthcare to low-income families. Until 2015 ARY Insurance covered 1,600+ surgeries and treated 3.1 lakh patients across 18 health centres in Karnataka.
  <sub>The CSR Universe · https://thecsruniverse.com/articles/biocon-foundation-marks-20-years-of-transforming-lives-through-impactful-social-initiatives · confidence high</sub>
- **Biocon Academy · programme**
  > Biocon Academy, the group's flagship initiative, focused on bridging the skills gap in the biopharma sector. Advanced training programs provided high-end education to equip students with industry-relevant skills.
  <sub>India CSR · https://indiacsr.in/biocon-groups-csr-spending-for-fy-2023-24-reaches-rs-31-54-crore · confidence high</sub>
- **Biocon Nagar · project · under Biocon Foundation**
  > Biocon Nagar: A sustainable housing project for safe homes, created for over 400 families displaced by floods.

  > Funding Metro Station: Funded the construction of Hebbagodi Metro Station, easing commute stress. Also transformed over 50 metro pillars from Huskur Gate to Hebbagodi with vibrant artwork.

- **Lake Rejuvenation (Hebbagodi & Yarandahalli Lakes) · programme · under Biocon Foundation**
  > Lake Rejuvenation: Restoration of Hebbagodi and Yarandahalli Lakes, with Hebbagodi Lake earning a Limca Book of Records mention for India's largest artificial floating island (12,000 sq. ft.). Miyawaki forests were planted with 3,500 saplings to aid afforestation.
